met_analysis:
The Depression (Remnant of Very Severe Cyclonic Storm “Arnab”) over south Chhattisgarh and adjoining south Odisha moved nearly northwards with the speed of 18 kmph during past 6 hours, and lies centered at 0830 hrs IST of today, the 29th October, over the same region near latitude 19.4°N and longitude 81.9°E, about 40 km north-northwest of Jagdalpur (Chhattisgarh), 180 km southwest of Titlagarh (Odisha), 150 km west- southwest of Bhawanipatna (Odisha), 200 km south of Raipur (Odisha), and 310 km southwest of Sambalpur (Odisha). It is very likely to continue to move nearly northwards, and weaken into a well marked low pressure area over North Chhattisgarh and adjoining Northwest Odisha around evening of today, the 29th October 2026.
The low pressure area over south Andaman Sea & neighbourhood persisted over the same region at 0830 Hrs IST of today, the 29th October 2026. The associated cyclonic circulation extends upto 7.6 km above mean sea level. It is very likely to move west-northwestwards and become a Well Marked Low Pressure Area over south Andaman Sea and adjoining Andaman & Nicobar Islands during next 24 hours. Thereafter, continuing to move west-northwestwards, it is very likely to concentrate into a depression over southeast Bay of Bengal and adjoining Andaman & Nicobar Islands and Andaman Sea during subsequent 24 hours.
The Western Disturbance as a cyclonic circulation over north Pakistan and neighbourhood between 3.1 and 4.5 km above mean sea level persists, with the trough aloft in middle & upper tropospheric westerlies with axis at 5.8 km above mean sea level now runs roughly along Long. 68°E to the north of Lat. 22°N.
An Induce upper air cyclonic circulation lies over south Punjab & neighbourhood at 1.5 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over south Konkan and neighbourhood extending upto 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
A trough runs from the cyclonic circulation associated with the depression over south Chhattisgarh and adjoining south Odisha to the cyclonic circulation over south Konkan across Telangana and North Interior Karnataka & extends upto 3.1 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Haryana & adjoining Uttar Pradesh lies over north Haryana & neighbourhood at 0.9 km above mean sea level.
